intendedProduct: Municipal-branded rainwater-based packaged drinking water, if legally authorized and compliant

legalClassification.candidateRoute: Real Decreto 1799/2010 governs prepared packaged drinking waters other than natural mineral and spring waters. Article 2 defines prepared waters as waters of any origin subjected to authorized physicochemical treatments necessary to meet Annex I potability characteristics. Whether this specific harvested rainwater source and proposed operating model fit the prepared packaged-water route requires written competent-authority/legal confirmation.
legalClassification.requiredBeforePilot: Written legal and competent-authority confirmation of source/product classification, operator/facility approvals, treatment requirements, sampling regime, naming and label rules.
regulatoryInterpretation: RD 1799/2010 is the primary candidate packaged-water framework, subject to legal classification and authorization.
RD 3/2023 excludes waters governed by RD 1799/2010 from its general scope, but RD 1799/2010 cross-references RD 3/2023's list of observation for prepared packaged waters.
Do not apply RD 3/2023 distribution-zone sampling schedules as a substitute for RD 1799/2010's packaged-water operator and finished-product controls.
Rainwater source, collection, treatment, source authorization, food-business registration and product naming must be confirmed with the competent Spanish authorities.

specificationPolicy: The competent-authority-approved product category and current legal specification must be versioned. Parameter names, limits, units, methods, sampling frequency and test scope must be sourced from the applicable current annex/authorization. No generic hard-coded limits are authoritative.
hardStops: Unapproved or expired laboratory accreditation scope
Missing legal classification or operator authorization
Batch volume or lot identity mismatch

packaging.note: Apply the regulation's phased obligations to the selected bottle/can material, design, food-contact requirements, recyclability, recycled content, labelling and producer responsibility as applicable.

releaseRule: AquaDMRV may evaluate readiness and record the authorized QA decision. No model, sensor, report generator or blockchain transaction can autonomously override a hold or release a product without the legally required human/operator authorization.

samplingSchedule.hardStop: Missing or nonconforming daily results hold the affected batch and trigger deviation review.
Overdue or missing periodic results block release of batches in the affected review window until assessed.
An overdue full analysis blocks release until compliance is restored.
An overdue or failed radiological assessment blocks release pending authority/QA review.

operationalQms: Take representative samples of product quality throughout the year at the packaging point.
Ensure laboratory technical competence and analytical result quality; retain laboratory identity, accreditation/competence scope, methods, units, detection limits and report identifiers.
Validate authorized physicochemical treatment, disinfection efficacy and treatment by-product controls.
Maintain cleanable/inspectable collection, conveyance, storage and filling circuits; retain cleaning, sanitation and maintenance records.
Use automated, hygienic filling and closure processes; retain fill-line and packaging-lot traceability.
Use closures designed to prevent falsification and contamination; reject cracked, broken or defective containers.
Register the food business operator in the applicable Spanish food-business register (RGSEAA) when required by the selected route.
labeling: Where the prepared packaged-water route is confirmed, use the legally required product denomination; RD 1799/2010 Article 8 specifies 'agua potable preparada' for prepared potable water from a spring or catchment.
The mandatory denomination must be visually more prominent than the brand or distinctive sign under the applicable Article 8 rule.
Municipal/Polideportivo branding must not mislead consumers about the source, origin, classification or nature of the water.
Never use 'natural mineral water' or 'spring water' unless the source and legal classification independently qualify.
